items.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
items.desc: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recordedMultiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains. Continue reading...

items.title: West Bank attacks: Opposition leader Eisenkot decries "Jewish terrorism"
items.desc: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were set on fire in three villages in the occupied West Bank. Israeli soldiers were deployed to the area following the attacks, which local residents said were carried out by Israeli settlers. Gadi Eisenkot, a rival of outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, condemned the acts on X, describing them as “Jewish terrorism”. Antonia Kerrigan reports.

items.title: Russian strike kills 2 in Kyiv
items.desc: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in the village of Dymer, just north of Kyiv, on Sunday, killing at least two people and wounding four others. The morning strike destroyed a five-storey building, while rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child. At least 11 others are believed to remain trapped under the rubble.

items.title: The week in pictures: Xi hosts Trump and Putin, COP31 and new French protests
items.desc: From the unprecedented Shenzhen summit in China that saw President Xi Jinping host his US and Russian counterparts, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, to tough talks at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey and another week of French protests over the cost of living, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the most striking images from the past week.

items.title: "It can take years": Why the AI Riemann proof is far from settled
items.desc: AI claimed another major scalp in maths on Friday, as Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge published what he says is a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a Millennium Prize Problem, in 17 million lines of code that no human has read in full. Physicist Tony Padilla tells Tech 24 that verification could take years, and that Alpöge should share how he got there.

items.title: Israel investigates West Bank fires
items.desc: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were vandalised and set on fire in four villages in the occupied West Bank, in attacks local activists say were carried out by Israeli settlers. Around eight vehicles were reportedly torched and racist slogans sprayed on walls, prompting Israeli soldiers and police to deploy to the area. The attacks come amid a surge in settler violence since the outbreak of the Gaza war in October 2023, with more than 1,100 Palestinians killed by Israeli soldiers or settlers in the West Bank since then, according to an AFP tally. They also follow recent sanctions announced by the UK and Australia against eight Israeli companies involved in settlement activity. France 24 correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky shares further details from Jerusalem.

items.title: 🔴 COP31 ends without deal as EU rejects text for omitting mention of fossil fuels
Indonesia factory hit by deadly blaze: Three killed and 36 missing
items.desc: At least three people have been killed and dozens are missing after a fire broke out at a factory in Indonesia producing sweets and snack products. Fifteen people were rescued alive from the plant, while firefighters were still battling flames in several parts of the facility more than 12 hours after the blaze began. The cause of the fire remains unknown, but survivors said it started in a cooling unit on the third floor.

items.title: Former Italian police chief found dead
items.desc: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has expressed shock following the death of a former national police chief, whose body was found on Saturday. He had been under investigation over an alleged cover-up in an inquiry into a bombing linked to organised crime in Sicily. Jennie Shin reports.

items.title: Princess of Wales opens up about cancer
items.desc: A new documentary titled Heal follows Britain’s Princess Catherine as she navigates life since her cancer diagnosis in 2024. The film tracks the 44-year-old as she attempts to climb the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours. In the trailer, she reflects on healing as a journey. Ophelie Jacobson reports.

items.title: South Korea: AI cheating sparks exam security chaos
items.desc: South Korea’s education minister resigned on Sunday following a major cheating scandal that erupted just ahead of the country’s university entrance exams. The controversy centred on the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam, who admitted to using a miniature camera and smartphone to secure a near-perfect result. Jack Pownall reports.

items.title: Europe sees new protests over rising costs, inequality and public services
items.desc: Sunday marks the third consecutive day of protests across Europe, following large demonstrations on Friday and smaller rallies on Saturday, from Portugal to France. The protests have largely focused on the rising cost of living and access to affordable housing. In France, demonstrations have now taken place for six weekends in a row. Ophelie Jacobson reports.

items.title: English village votes to "leave UK"
items.desc: Residents of the small English village of Barnham voted on Saturday in a symbolic referendum to leave the UK, in protest against government plans to house 931 asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base – more than the village’s own population of 584. The vote follows a similar protest in another village in September, highlighting growing tensions over immigration across the country. Earlier this week, the leader of a far-right anti-immigration group was jailed, but supporters have vowed to keep the movement alive. Jack Pownall reports.

items.title: NATO faces sovereignty dilemma as militaries rely on private tech, AI
items.desc: NATO officials and defence experts gathered at the NATO Edge conference in Turkey this week to discuss how militaries can harness artificial intelligence and high tech without compromising control over sensitive data and defence capabilities.

items.title: Live: Ukrainian rescuers search for survivors in rubble after Russian attack
items.desc: Ukrainian rescue teams on Sunday searched for survivors in the rubble of a collapsed residential building in Dymer, in the Kyiv region, after a Russian drone strike, which killed two people and wounded four others. Meanwhile, Finland warned the war was "spilling over" after a drone set fire to a Russian cargo ship in the Baltic Sea Saturday. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

items.title: South Korean education minister resigns over AI-driven exam cheating scandal
items.desc: South Korea Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned Sunday over an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted days before the high-stakes Suneung university entrance exam. The Suneung concluded "without any major incidents" last week, Choi said, but he admitted to a failure to "prepare adequately in advance".

items.title: Bahrain accuses Iran of striking industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz
items.desc: Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial site on Saturday evening, as two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran reported shooting down a US drone amid stalled efforts to end the war.

items.title: EU-Indonesia agreement sees the light after ten years of negotiations
items.desc: The European Union and Indonesia have signed a major trade deal, ten years after talks began.The agreement removes almost all tariffs between the EU and Southeast Asia's biggest economy: 98.5 per cent of them. For Europe, it means access to a market of 280 million people and a steadier supply of nickel for batteries. For Indonesia, easier exports of palm oil, textiles and footwear, and it arrives just before its current EU trade preferences end on the 1st of January. To discuss the deal Airlangga Hartarto, Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs in Indonesia joined us on the programme.

items.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for ‘marathon’ Israeli coalition talks
items.desc: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has invited caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party for coalition talks, his centrist Yashar party said Saturday. The "marathon series of talks" starts Sunday, the party said, adding that the move reflected a commitment to form "the broadest possible government" after the October election failed to deliver an outright winner.

items.title: France’s sixth consecutive Saturday of protests draws lower turnout
items.desc: Turnout ⁠was down ​at largely peaceful demonstrations across France on the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests ​over the cost of living, with the interior ministry putting the figure at 82,500 across the country. Organisers said 150,000 people participated in the nationwide protests, down from their 200,000 figure last week.

items.title: 'Worst Ever' COP Summit?
items.desc:
Is this the worst COP summit on record?
 
With limited political leadership, no official US delegation and mounting frustration over bureaucratic delays, questions are being raised about the effectiveness of the climate negotiations.
 
Juan Carlos Beldsoe, a former White House climate adviser under Bill Clinton, described the process as labyrinthine and ultimately dispiriting.
 
France 24's Gavin Lee speaks with climate advocate and six-time COP delegate, Henna Hundal about what this means for the future of global climate action.

items.title: Russia attacks Zelensky's hometown, Ukraine reaffirms wish to join NATO
items.desc: A Russian ballistic missile attack on President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday killed two people and wounded dozens. Hours later, Zelensky reiterated his country's determination to join NATO, following proposals to provide Kyiv with security guarantees similar to those of the military alliance.

items.title: Russia launches ballistic missile attack on Zelensky's hometown in central Ukraine
items.desc: A Russian ballistic missile attack on President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday killed two people and wounded dozens. Hours later, Zelensky reiterated his country's determination to join NATO. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kyiv.

items.title: 【前方视野】1.5摄氏度临界点逼近：中国如何回答气候变化时代的转型之问
items.desc: 从工业革命以来，人类从未像今天这样清晰地感受到自身活动与地球系统之间的关联。持续刷新的高温纪录、愈发频繁的极端天气，都在提醒国际社会，应对气候变化的窗口正在收窄。在土耳其举行的第31届联合国气候变化框架公约缔约方大会（COP31）上，各国围绕减排目标、能源转型、气候融资和绿色贸易展开激烈讨论。面对全球升温可能在未来十年内跨越1.5摄氏度关键门槛的警示，中国国家气候变化专家委员会副主任王毅在接受《联合国新闻》专访时表示，气候行动已进入更加注重落实的新阶段，而中国正在通过全面绿色转型、新型能源体系建设、绿色低碳技术创新及法律制度建设，为长期绿色低碳发展探索了一条具有自身特色的路径。

items.title: 约旦河西岸：定居者袭击事件创纪录  联合国敦促以色列保护农民
items.desc: 联合国机构和人道主义非政府组织周五表示，在今年被占领的约旦河西岸橄榄收获季期间，以色列定居者发动了400多次袭击，造成人员伤亡或财产损失——这一数字超过了以往任何一个收获季。

items.title: 粮食署计划2027年援助9100万人
items.desc: 世界粮食计划署周五表示，计划在2027年为9100万人提供援助，需要121亿美元资金。该机构警告，资金持续短缺将使更多人陷入饥饿，新一轮全球粮食危机可能正在逼近。

items.title: 教科文组织：学前教育每投入1美元，到2035年可获近4美元回报
items.desc: 联合国教科文组织周五发布报告指出，过去十年，全球学前教育普及几乎停滞不前。进入小学的儿童中，仅约六成接受过至少一年的学前教育。资金不足和持续存在的不平等，使数百万幼儿难以获得优质保育和教育。

items.title: 支离破碎的游乐场和冰冷的教室：乌克兰儿童遭遇最惨重的一年
items.desc: 在基辅一所两度遭轰炸的幼儿园废墟中，停电已持续一整天。联合国儿童基金会周五指出，随着儿童伤亡人数攀升至创纪录水平，在乌克兰度过又一个严酷冬天的儿童正面临巨大危险。

items.title: 阿富汗的限制措施阻碍孕妇寻求医疗救助
items.desc: 阿富汗援助与发展机构周五警告称，针对妇女和女童权利与自由的侵犯行为日益加剧，这导致越来越多的妇女和女童无法获得至关重要的医疗护理。

items.title: 联合国危机教育全球基金拨款5200万美元 助力30万儿童继续学习

items.title: COP31原定闭幕日到来，多国要求明确摆脱化石燃料并加强资金支持
items.desc: 周五是第31届联合国气候变化大会原定闭幕日，来自欧洲、非洲、拉丁美洲和太平洋地区的多个国家联合要求修改协议草案，明确逐步摆脱化石燃料的行动方向，并加强气候资金支持。谈判代表仍在努力寻找近200个国家都能接受的方案。

items.title: 【子午播报】2026年11月20日
items.desc: 纽约时间零点，北京时间13点，欢迎收看《联合国子午播报》。本期节目您将看到，中美俄深圳会晤，联合国如何回应？国际法院认定缅甸对罗兴亚人实施种族灭绝。子午聚焦：联合国讨论管制“杀人机器人”。

items.title: 【专题报道 | 前方视野】从“丢弃”迈向“循环“时代：零废弃物议程试图打开气候行动的新突破口
items.desc: 在联合国气候变化大会的谈判大厅里，焦点往往集中在能源转型、气候融资和减排目标上。然而，正在土耳其安塔利亚举行的第31届气候变化大会凸显了气候行动中一个长期被低估的领域：通过减少废弃物和推动循环经济来实现减排，这些举措正在成为减缓全球变暖见效快、成本低且极具现实可行性的突破口之一。

items.title: 联合国警告：人工智能正被用于诱骗和剥削儿童
items.desc: 联合国周四警告，人工智能正被侵害者和犯罪团伙用于诱骗、勒索和剥削儿童，而相应保护措施未能跟上技术发展的步伐。

items.title: 联合国：全球电子政务持续推进  但数字鸿沟依然存在
items.desc: 联合国经济和社会事务部周四发布的《2026年联合国电子政务调查报告》指出，全球数字政府发展持续推进，但网络连接、技能和机构能力方面的差距仍在限制数字化带来的效益。随着人工智能重塑公共行政，各国在电子政务发展方面的不平衡依然明显。

items.title: COP31：最新协议草案删去摆脱化石燃料相关表述
items.desc: 第31届联合国气候变化大会原定闭幕前夕，最新协议草案删去了逐步摆脱化石燃料的明确表述，引发民间团体不满。各方周四继续就资金、适应和公正转型等关键议题磋商，力争在周五前弥合分歧。

items.title: 国际法院认定缅甸对罗兴亚人实施种族灭绝
items.desc: 国际法院周四就冈比亚诉缅甸案作出判决，认定缅甸在2017年若开邦北部的军事清剿行动中，对罗兴亚人实施了种族灭绝。这是该院首次认定一个国家须为实施种族灭绝承担责任。

items.title: 粮农组织：全球粮食供应总体充裕 但市场风险和粮食安全挑战加剧
items.desc: 联合国粮食及农业组织周四发布最新一期《粮食展望》报告指出，全球农产品供应总体充裕，特别是小麦和粗粮，但大米、食糖和植物油的供需平衡趋于紧张。天气变化、物流中断和政策不确定性正增加全球粮食市场风险。同日，粮农组织总干事屈冬玉呼吁加强国际合作，将粮食安全纳入预防和解决冲突的外交努力。

items.title: 货币基金组织总裁：人工智能将成为影响全球竞争力和经济增长的重要因素
items.desc: 国际货币基金组织总裁格奥尔基耶娃周四在中国深圳举行的2026年亚太经合组织经济领导人会议上表示，人工智能正在对全球经济增长产生实质性影响，将成为影响中期竞争力、生产率和经济增长的重要因素。她同时指出，全球通胀上升、公共债务增加以及结构性改革滞后等问题仍对经济前景构成挑战，各国需要加快采取政策行动。

items.title: 联合国人口基金警告：世界正面临辜负下一代的风险
items.desc: 联合国人口基金周三发布的《2026年世界人口状况报告》指出，尽管年轻一代的教育水平、信息获取能力以及对自身权利的认知达到前所未有的高度，但经济不稳定、不平等、排斥、冲突和气候变化等因素，正阻碍数以百万计的年轻人实现人生抱负，使他们难以获得体面的工作、经济独立、住房以及建立家庭的机会。

items.title: 第31届气候变化大会僵局持续，各国启动新一轮“气候承诺核查”
items.desc: 随着在土耳其安塔利亚举行的第31届联合国气候变化大会闭幕时限日益临近，各国于周三启动了一项新的全球性核查，以检验气候承诺是否得到履行。与此同时，各国部长在峰会的一些最棘手问题上仍陷于僵局：谁来买单、全球摆脱化石燃料的速度有多快，以及如果较贫穷国家无力承担，更绿色的未来能否被称为“公正”。

items.title: 经巴拿马北上人流减少九成，拉美移民转向新路线
items.desc: 国际移民组织周三发布报告指出，2026年上半年，经巴拿马达连隘口北上的移民人数较去年同期下降90%。与此同时，部分移民转而南下、返乡或在其他国家定居，拉丁美洲和加勒比地区的迁徙路线与目的地正在发生变化。

items.title: 儿基会：全球每四分钟就有一名儿童死于暴力
items.desc: 第二届消除针对儿童的暴力问题全球部长级会议周三在菲律宾马尼拉召开。联合国儿童基金会呼吁各国，将两年前在波哥大作出的承诺转化为持续投入，推广已被证明有效的措施，保护儿童免遭暴力侵害。

items.title: 也门战事升级导致至少128名儿童伤亡
items.desc: 联合国儿童基金会周三表示，自9月3日也门战事升级以来，至少已有64名儿童死亡、64名儿童受伤。随着塔伊兹、拉赫季等人口密集地区周边战斗持续，伤亡人数可能进一步上升。

items.title: 原子能机构：伊朗核查工作陷入停滞 乌克兰核设施安全风险持续加剧
items.desc: 国际原子能机构总干事格罗西周三在维也纳向理事会介绍机构工作情况时表示，伊朗核查监督工作因无法获取相关信息和进入核设施而陷入停滞，乌克兰军事冲突持续威胁核设施安全，朝鲜核计划也在进一步推进。与此同时，全球核电发展势头增强，原子能机构将继续推动核能和平利用和核技术国际合作。

items.title: 美国等三国麻疹持续传播，泛美卫生组织呼吁加强疫苗接种

items.title: COP31：海洋保护进入谈判议程，落实承诺仍需资金支持

items.title: 各国承诺加快肥胖防治 力争2030年降低5%患病率

items.title: 苏丹：联合国报告详述无人机袭击激增对平民造成的致命影响

items.title: 冬雨加剧加沙人道危机，援助受限与资金短缺阻碍救援
